9.22: The Hebrew calls the recipients “them” and has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB names “the Gibeonites” and gives a single “said.”
9.23: The Hebrew uses the image of a servant not being “cut off from among you”; BSB expresses this as serving perpetually.
9.24: The Hebrew leaves the speakers unnamed, explicitly names Joshua, and repeats “the land” in its inhabitants clause; BSB names “The Gibeonites,” leaves Joshua implicit, and uses “its inhabitants.”
9.25: The Hebrew has singular “your hand” and says “in your eyes”; BSB has plural “your hands” and “seems ... to you.”
9.26: The Hebrew begins with an unnamed “he,” has singular “the hand of the sons of Israel,” and ends with “them”; BSB names Joshua, uses plural “hands,” and explicitly names the Gibeonites.
9.27: The Hebrew explicitly names Joshua and says “for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD”; BSB uses “he” and attaches “of the LORD” to “congregation.”
